title: Results directory retention: extend operation prune to spilled query outputs
description: Context: a 2h47m dabble-employee-app agent session made 300 CLI calls with 24 failures. Failure clusters: 117 read-only work show polls (~40% of all calls), 14 identical failed sync refresh retries, 6 vault init retries, 66 agent finish calls with only 2 standalone evidence records, 6 NOT_FOUND finish/release (ownership confusion), 1 CONFLICT claim, 2 POLICY_VIOLATION sprint closes. Design principle for this mission: every response (success or error) must carry enough state that the correct next action is derivable without another read, and the honest path (evidence, ownership, health) must be the path of least resistance. Problem: --json calls exceeding the inline size cap spill full results to .boreal/results/; these are transient query outputs but nothing prunes them (63 orphaned files in the audited repo, contributing to a 155MB .boreal). Change: extend the existing operation prune command to also age out results files past a retention window (default suggestion 7 days), and have doctor report the results directory size and stale-file count as an informational finding. Where: operation prune handler in apps/cli/src/commands.ts, doctor findings. Constraint: never prune ledgers, runtime state, or anything outside results/; prune must be safe while another command is writing a new result file (skip files younger than a grace period).
acceptanceCriteria: operation prune removes results files older than the retention window and reports what it removed
doctor reports results directory size and stale-file count
Files younger than the grace period and everything outside results/ are never touched
